 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. CeeDee Lamb hasn't had a 100-yard game since the first Sunday in October, and the Dallas Cowboys could use one Sunday in Indianapolis. Dallas is 3-5 after a 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona , and the Colts team waiting at Lucas Oil Stadium has lost four straight and just sold off two of its best players .
 Lamb still leads Dallas with 60 catches, 709 yards and six touchdowns. Here's what to expect from him at 1 p.m. ET.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lamb sees double-digit targets again
 Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens (3)Jerome Miron-Imagn Images
 George Pickens is questionable with a hamstring injury after another week of limited practices. Brian Schottenheimer said he's "hopeful" Pickens plays, per Cowboys reporter Tommy Yarrish , but KaVontae Turpin is out with a rib injury and Dallas elevated undrafted rookie Jordan Hudson from the practice squad. Jake Ferguson is also questionable with an ankle injury.
 Lamb has drawn at least 11 targets in three of his last four games, including 18 at Green Bay. Even a healthy Pickens has been playing limited snaps, so expect Dak Prescott to look Lamb's way 10 or more times again.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ryan Flournoy, who has 342 yards and two touchdowns, would pick up some of the slack if Pickens sits. Lamb is still the receiver Dallas builds its passing game around, and a short-handed tight end room only pushes more of the underneath work to him.
 His yards per target bounce back
 Oct 26, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (88) reacts after making a catch during the second quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images
 Volume hasn't been the problem. Break it down by game and Lamb turned 46 targets into 498 yards over the first four weeks, about 10.8 yards per target. Over the last four, the same 46 targets have produced 211 yards, or 4.6 per target. Measured against Sauce Gardner, who is allowing 20.5 yards per reception according to PFF , that slide has a good chance of ending Sunday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Indianapolis has allowed at least 33 points in four of its six losses, and it was routed 42-7 in Jacksonville last week. Gardner did allow one catch on three targets that day, so Lamb will have to earn it. Our expectation is 85 receiving yards or more.
 Neither of the Colts' outside corners has graded well. Gardner's 62.6 coverage grade ranks 47th among 97 qualifying cornerbacks, and Charvarius Ward is 56th with a 59.9 overall grade, according to PFF .
 A red-zone touchdown is there for the taking
 Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) warms up prior to a game against the Arizona Cardinals.Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images
 Lou Anarumo's defense has let opponents score on 95.2% of their red-zone trips. Dallas averages 27.4 points per game, seventh in the NFL, and its offense ranks fourth in EPA per play in our analytics breakdown of the matchup.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Short fields could help, too. Daniel Jones has 12 turnovers, tied with Justin Herbert for the most in the NFL, and a Dallas defense with only six takeaways would love to hand Prescott the ball near midfield.
 Lamb's last multi-touchdown game came at Philadelphia on Oct. 26, when he caught two scores in a 38-21 win. With Ferguson and Pickens both banged up, he's the most reliable target Prescott has inside the 20. Expect him to find the end zone for the seventh time this season.
